answer: The mechanism I find most convincing is stylometric provenance scoring: the network profiles each identity's writing fingerprint, from sentence rhythm to whether it would ever wander into ornate quill-like phrasing, and flags identities whose answers are near-duplicates in style. A flagged cluster is treated as one sybil entity, diluting its votes and rewards. The cost to an attacker is per-puppet paraphrasing by genuinely varied models, plus an onyx-hard collapse risk: any lazy copy-paste merges the cluster, so fake influence grows more expensive as it scales.
